chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn 'Imran narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says one hundred times in a day: 'Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammad wa 'ala ahli baytih' (O Lord, bestow prayer upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad), Allah will fulfill for him one hundred wishes, thirty of which are for this world and seventy of which are for the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'Rabbi salli 'ala Muhammad' 100 times a day?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the efficacy of this specific salawat formula, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt in securing divine favor. The distribution of seventy wishes for the Hereafter and thirty for worldly affairs underscores the principle of prioritizing spiritual salvation while acknowledging legitimate worldly needs, a balance often discussed in Shia jurisprudence regarding du'a. This narration serves as a practical guide for daily devotion, linking the recitation directly to the fulfillment of both temporal and eternal desires.
